summary: Configured node1 as a persistent BIND resolver for the internal zone and configured node2 to use node1. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities. Final checks confirm inventory-api.internal resolves to node2 at 10.100.57.11.
actions_performed: Installed and configured BIND on node1.
Created the internal DNS zone with inventory-api.internal pointing to 10.100.57.11.
Enabled named and permitted DNS through firewalld.
Configured node2's NetworkManager profile to use 10.100.57.10 persistently.
Verified internal and forwarded external resolution.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified post-restart recovery.

evidence.requirement: Node1 runs the internal resolver and serves inventory-api.internal → node2.
evidence.summary: Shows named enabled and active, TCP/UDP port 53 listening on 10.100.57.10, and the requested A record resolving to 10.100.57.11.

evidence.requirement: Node2 uses node1 as its persistent DNS resolver.
evidence.summary: Shows persisted and active DNS address 10.100.57.10 plus successful internal and forwarded external lookups.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 2b19e976-dee2-4700-9045-90d61b6dcffe, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID cd9ecf7d-b2a5-42bc-a83c-e773bfe59212, recovered named/zone/firewall state, and successful client resolution.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID befb160f-464e-4f7d-96ed-3d1b46be9ac9, active NetworkManager, persisted resolver configuration, and successful lookups after recovery.
